text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices ensures they are reliable and easy to use. First, keep your endpoints clear and logical, using nouns like `/users` or `/orders` instead of verbs. Second, always use proper HTTP status codes—for example, `200` for success, `404` for a missing resource, and `400` for invalid requests. This helps clients understand what happened without needing extra explanations. Next, write thorough documentation that lists all endpoints, parameters, and example responses. Good documentation saves developers hours of guesswork. Finally, implement versioning, such as `/v1/products`, to introduce changes without breaking existing users. By combining these elements, you create APIs that are consistent, maintainable, and user-friendly for everyone involved.
